name: Brazil
gaps: WikiAves (citizen science platform) could not be URL-verified due to Cloudflare access restrictions, though it is clearly active and is the primary birding platform in Brazil.
Several regional clubs lack active websites and maintain only social media presence (e.g., COA Santos on Instagram, COACGR on Facebook).
Some older URLs from ABOA directory (Multiply, Yahoo Groups, Geocities) are no longer accessible.

Dropped for having no presence of their own, each pointing at the same national COA directory rather than a page of its own: Vem Passarinhar Sampa (São Paulo); Observadores de Aves de Ubatuba (São Paulo); COA Foz do Iguaçu (Paraná); OAA (Paraná); COAVE (Santa Catarina); Santa Catarina Birdwatching (Santa Catarina); Projeto Charão (Rio Grande do Sul); Projeto Cardeal Amarelo (Rio Grande do Sul); Avis Vigilanti (Minas Gerais); COA-JF (Minas Gerais); S.O.S. Falconiformes (Minas Gerais); Amigos das Aves (Rio de Janeiro); Clube de Observadores de Aves da Bahia (Bahia); ANO (Bahia)
Dropped as a global platform rather than a local community (listed once under International): eBird Brasil
Dropped, link dead when checked on 2026-08-09: COAB (São Paulo)

Amazonas: tested directly rather than assumed. Vem Passarinhar Manaus is a real bird walk programme run by the Universidade do Estado do Amazonas with a named coordinator and Global Big Day participation, but it only has dated news posts on the university's site, no landing page of its own, and an Instagram handle whose bio and follower count could not be independently confirmed in any search result, so no card was added.

Para: tested directly rather than assumed. Clube de Observacao de Aves do Para (COAPA), founded 2024 with about 280 members and covered by Diario do Para, has no findable website or independently verifiable social page. A related Bora Passarinhar guide training project at UFOPA in Santarem, working toward a Tapajos bird club, is also real but has no confirmable page of its own. Both states show genuine club level activity forming, contradicting the earlier assumption that it is purely tourism and guide based, but neither has a verifiable link to publish yet.

Roraima: Clube de Observacao de Aves de Roraima (COA/RR), founded 2019 with about 41 members and led by Ronilson Moura Cavalcante, is confirmed real by independent press (Folha BV, Norte Extremo) but has no findable website or verifiable social page of its own.
Rondonia: no bird club or group found. Porto Velho markets itself as a birdwatching and sport fishing destination, but this is municipal tourism promotion, not a club or community with its own page.
Acre: no bird club or group with an independent online presence found, despite real ecotourism potential in the state's avifauna being discussed in local press.
Amapa: no bird club or group with an independent online presence found.
Maranhao: no bird club or group with an independent online presence found. UFMA runs birdwatching tourism training in local communities, but this is a training course, not a membership club.
Piaui: only a one off event, Bora Passarinhar Teresina at UFPI (first edition), was found; no ongoing club, group page or second edition turned up in search.

Paraiba: Clube Ornitologico da Paraiba (COPB) has its own site but is a captive breeding club for native species (Azulao, Curio, Trinca ferro and similar), regulated aviculture rather than birdwatching, so it was excluded as out of scope.
Alagoas: no bird club or group with an independent online presence found beyond a passing news mention of a general Sociedade Ornitologica de Alagoas with no verifiable page.
Sergipe: no bird club or group with an independent online presence found.

Tocantins: no bird club or group with an independent online presence found, despite Palmas and the Araguaia and Jalapao regions being recognised birding destinations with an active WikiAves observer base.

groups.name: SBO
groups.blurb: Sociedade Brasileira de Ornitologia, the national ornithological society founded in 1987, advancing Brazilian ornithology through congresses.

groups.name: ABOA
groups.blurb: Associação Brasileira de Observadores de Aves, national association founded 2011 bringing together birders across Brazil with resources and coordination.

groups.name: SAVE Brasil
groups.blurb: The BirdLife International partner in Brazil, conservation focused organisation operating in ten states with habitat restoration and community engagement.

groups.name: COA Brasil
groups.blurb: National movement and support network for bird observers across Brazil, connecting local clubs and enthusiasts practicing bird observation.

groups.name: Vem Passarinhar
groups.blurb: Nationwide initiative promoting free public bird watching outings in parks and protected areas.

groups.name: OBSERVAVES
groups.blurb: Observadores de Aves do Planalto Central, group founded 2005 promoting birdwatching in the Federal District through training and field excursions.

groups.name: Clube das Aves
groups.blurb: Student organization at Universidade Católica de Brasília dedicated to bird watching and ornithological studies for university community and students.

groups.name: OIA
groups.blurb: Observadores de aves de Goiás, group created by UFG professors and researchers to promote the state's bird fauna and environmental education.

groups.name: GOA Sinop
groups.blurb: Grupo de Observadores de Aves de Sinop, regional group in northern Mato Grosso involved in bird observation and community engagement.

groups.name: COA Campo Grande
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves de Campo Grande, regional bird watching club in Mato Grosso do Sul with active community participation.

groups.name: CEO
groups.blurb: Centro de Estudos Ornitológicos, one of Brazil's longest established ornithological societies founded 1985, conducting censuses and research in São Paulo.

groups.name: COAPI
groups.blurb: Clube de Observação de Aves do Parque Ibirapuera, group based at the iconic São Paulo park offering bird observation education and guided activities.

groups.name: Clube de Observadores de Aves Sesc São Paulo
groups.blurb: Bird watching club run by Sesc in São Paulo providing club activities, field trips and bird observation opportunities for members and visitors.

groups.name: COAVAP
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves do Vale do Paraíba, regional group serving the Paraíba Valley region of São Paulo state.

groups.name: COAFRANCA
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves de Franca, Sesc program running community bird observation and Global Bird Day celebrations at Unesp.

groups.name: GOA Jundiaí
groups.blurb: Grupo de Observação de Aves de Jundiaí, community group for bird observation in the city of Jundiaí.

groups.name: Associação Viçosense de Observadores de Aves
groups.blurb: Bird watching association based in Viçosa region, connecting local birders for field observations and species documentation.

groups.name: COAMA
groups.blurb: Clube dos Observadores de Aves da Mata Atlântica, group focused on Atlantic Forest bird observation in the region.

groups.name: Observando Aves na Cidade de São Paulo
groups.blurb: Public Facebook group for birders observing and sharing bird sightings in São Paulo city, with active community discussion.

groups.name: GOA Campinas
groups.blurb: Grupo de Observadores de Aves de Campinas, regional group in the city of Campinas for bird observation and community participation.

groups.name: COA-NPR
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves Norte do Paraná, regional club in northern Paraná active in Global Big Day and bird observation events.

groups.name: COA Joinville
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves de Joinville e Regiao, well established regional club in Santa Catarina running walks and community activities.

groups.name: COA-POA
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves de Porto Alegre, the first COA founded in Brazil in 1984, with decades of bird observation and field work.

groups.name: ECOAVIS
groups.blurb: Ecologia e Observação de Aves de Belo Horizonte, group dedicated to bird ecology and observation in Minas Gerais with research focus.

groups.name: COA-ES
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves do Espírito Santo, regional club maintaining a directory of COA clubs across Brazil on their website.

groups.name: AMOAVES
groups.blurb: Associação dos Observadores de Aves de Domingos Martins, local group in Espírito Santo for bird observation and community engagement.

groups.name: COA-RJ
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves Rio de Janeiro, founded 1985, one of Brazil's oldest COA clubs with active field work and community programs.

groups.name: COA Sul-Fluminense
groups.blurb: Clube dos observadores de aves do Sul Fluminense, regional group for the southern region of Rio de Janeiro state.

groups.name: LORMA
groups.blurb: Laboratório de Ornitologia e Mastozoologia at UEFS, academic research group conducting ornithological studies and bird monitoring in Bahia.

groups.name: OAP
groups.blurb: Observadores de Aves de Pernambuco, group established 1986 bringing together amateur bird observers across the state.

groups.name: Projeto Vem Passarinhar Recife
groups.blurb: Free public monthly bird watching initiative coordinated by environmental activist Ludmila Portela, running guided tours in Recife parks with provided binoculars.

groups.name: Projeto Vem Passarinhar CE
groups.blurb: Initiative launched 2019 organizing free monthly public bird watching outings at Cocó Park and across Ceará's protected areas for community environmental education.

groups.name: GOP
groups.blurb: Grupo Ornitológico Potiguar, founded 2007 in Natal, group conducting ornithological research and documentation of Rio Grande do Norte birds.
